headline: Local Man Spends 14 Hours Trying To Extinguish Birthday Diya With A Magnifying Glass To Prove He Is A Secularist
body:
Ramesh Kumar, a resident of Lajpat Nagar, was spotted sweating profusely on his balcony this afternoon while attempting to focus direct sunlight through a magnifying glass onto a single 'Aashirwad ka Diya' he had lit earlier in compliance with party directives. Kumar, who claims he identifies as a 'militant centrist,' spent the better part of his day trying to extinguish the candle without actually touching it, citing a need to preserve his household's ideological neutrality.

"It’s not that I don’t respect the sentiment, it’s just that I need to maintain a very specific level of public indifference to remain employable in my office’s open-plan seating arrangement," said Kumar, while shielding his DIY experiment from the gaze of his neighbor, who was busy arranging twenty-four lamps in the shape of a lotus. "If I don't put this out, the guys at work will assume I’ve started a new personal narrative, and I honestly don't have the energy to justify my morning routine before the first coffee break."

Witnesses report that Kumar’s attempts were largely unsuccessful, as the midday heat simply caused the diya’s wax to pool more effectively, resulting in a flame that grew brighter by the hour. By 4:00 PM, a small crowd of local tea-stall regulars had gathered to observe the spectacle, with many offering Kumar helpful, if conflicting, advice on how to blow out a candle without losing his political standing in the colony.
caption: Living your best, most confusing political life in the city. Tag a friend who tries this hard to stay neutral in the WhatsApp group. #DiyaDrama #NeutralityIssues #BirthdayVibes #LajpatNagar (satire)
igHook: Would you go to these lengths just to stay 'neutral' in your group chat?
